articles.title: Jeffrey Donaldson: 'No reports' made to Stormont review
articles.summary: A review by the assembly into Donaldson's conduct during his time at Stormont has found "no relevant information".
articles.body:
A review by the Northern Ireland Assembly into Jeffrey Donaldson's conduct during his time at Stormont has found "no relevant information" requiring further investigation.

No reports were received as part of the exercise, which was commissioned in July following the former Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader's conviction for child sex offences.

Donaldson was convicted in June of 18 counts of sex abuse including one count of rape, which he committed against two women when they were children. Donaldson is to appeal .

The Northern Ireland Assembly said the review was "necessarily limited" and "does not determine that no incidents occurred", but added the process had "now concluded".

Donaldson was a member of the legislative assembly (MLA) from 2003 until 2010 and at one point a junior minister in Northern Ireland's power-sharing government.

In subsequent years he was often a visitor at Stormont in his role as an MP and DUP leader.

The assembly's speaker Edwin Poots asked its chief executive to conduct the review.

It aimed to enable any current or former MLAs or staff, or other users of Parliament Buildings, to report "any incidents of abuse or inappropriate behaviour they directly experienced".

In a statement an assembly spokesperson said the review "has now concluded".

"No reports were received through the dedicated review contact route and no relevant information was identified through the internal information search," they said.

"The report therefore concludes that no matter has arisen within the scope of the review requiring further investigation, referral to the PSNI (Police Service of Northern Ireland), or referral to another statutory agency."

The assembly spokesperson said the report, which has been published online , was "clear that this conclusion is necessarily limited".

"The absence of reports or relevant records does not determine that no incidents occurred," they added.

"It means that, within the scope and methodology of the review, none were reported to the review and no relevant information was identified."

The assembly said any subsequent approach received would be handled under Assembly Commission policies and procedures "with urgent referral to the PSNI or another statutory agency where appropriate".

The review was one of several launched in the wake of Donaldson's conviction.

The DUP commissioned Jim Gamble, a child safety expert and former senior police officer, to lead an independent review into Donaldson's behaviour while he was in the party .

Staff in the Northern Ireland Civil Service have been asked to come forward with any experiences of abuse or inappropriate behaviour during Donaldson's time as a junior minister.

The Ulster Unionist Party (UUP), of which Donaldson was previously a member, also said it would appoint an external organisation for people to confidentially share any information .

articles.title: Meet Kiran Reddy, the 18-year-old Georgia teen who became the first Indian American to win Miss Teen USA
articles.summary: US News: An 18-year-old student from Douglas, Georgia, has made history by becoming the first Indian American to win the national Miss Teen USA crown. Kiran Re.
articles.body: An 18-year-old student from Douglas, Georgia, has made history by becoming the first Indian American to win the national Miss Teen USA crown. Kiran Reddy defeated 50 other contestants during the 44th annual pageant, held at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts in Miami, Florida, on 26 August 2026, according to WALB News and Pageant Circle. Reddy, who had earlier become the first Indian American to win the Miss Georgia Teen USA title, also secured Georgia’s first national victory in the pageant’s history. Her win marks a double milestone for diversity and state representation in the long-running beauty contest.Speaking after her victory, Reddy shared her emotions about taking on the prestigious title. "I am so blessed to represent Georgia and the U.S. and be the role model I always needed growing up," Reddy said, as reported by KFI AM 640. The national finals brought together contestants from all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Raquel Olea of Arkansas was named first runner-up, while Elisa Akin of New York, Kiersten Alvarado of Indiana, and Chloe Bella Dietz of Texas completed the top five. The event was hosted by model Sean Michael Rae and former titleholder Noelia Voigt. Last year’s winner, Mailyn Marsh of Missouri, placed the crown on her successor. The judging panel included notable figures such as Kelsey Swanson, a former Miss Rhode Island USA.Academic background and roots in GeorgiaBefore gaining national attention, Reddy achieved academic success in Coffee County, Georgia. She graduated as the valedictorian of Coffee High School in Douglas. After graduating from high school, Reddy enrolled at the University of Georgia, where she is studying biological sciences on a pre-medical track. Her goal of working in healthcare has been an important part of her platform alongside her pageant career. Reddy’s journey in pageantry has taken years of hard work. She entered competitive pageants at the age of 15. She finished as first runner-up at the Miss Georgia Teen USA contest in 2024, followed by a second runner-up finish in 2025. Her path to the national title began in June 2026, when she was appointed Miss Georgia Teen USA through an open casting call organised by the national pageant organisation, according to reports by WALB and Wikipedia.Cultural impact and upcoming international stageReddy’s historic victory highlights the growing representation of Indian Americans in US beauty pageants. As the first Indian American teenager to win the national crown, her achievement has attracted attention from community leaders and pageant fans around the world. Her duties as Miss Teen USA will soon include international representation. Reddy is scheduled to represent the United States at the Miss Teen Universe contest in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, in October 2026. This will be the first time the national organisation participates in the global event. Along with international travel and official appearances, Reddy plans to continue her undergraduate pre-med studies at the University of Georgia while carrying out her duties as Miss Teen USA.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2023, fire destroyed a Michigan school built in 1867, leaving only its brick facade; 3 years later, the site has reopened as a $175,000 public park
articles.summary: US News: A historic school building in Niles, Michigan, was destroyed in a devastating fire in 2023, only the iconic brick facade of the 1867 building remains..
articles.body: A historic school building in Niles, Michigan, was destroyed in a devastating fire in 2023, only the iconic brick facade of the 1867 building remains. For many residents, the loss felt like the end of an era for a site that had served as a school, community hub and local landmark for more than 150 years. But instead of letting the property sit vacant or selling it for redevelopment, the city and community partners chose a different path. Three years after the fire, the site has reopened as Ferry Street Memorial Park, a $175,000 public green space that honours the building’s history while giving neighbourhood residents a place to gather, play and remember. Local outlets, including the WSJM and the Southwestern Michigan College business community, have covered the transformation from burned-out shell to beloved new park.A school that anchored a neighbourhoodThe original Ferry Street School was built in 1867, during a period of rapid growth in Niles as railroads, industry and agriculture transformed the region. Over the decades, the building educated generations of local children, hosted community meetings and became a visual anchor for the surrounding neighbourhood. Even as the school’s educational use ended and the building aged, its brick facade and recognisable silhouette remained a point of pride for many residents. When the fire broke out, the building was no longer a school, but it still held great emotional and historical significance. In 2023, a fire gutted the interior, causing so much damage that the building could not be repaired. Only the exterior brick walls survived, standing as a hollow reminder of what had been lost.Deciding the future of a scarred siteIn the months after the fire, the city of Niles faced a difficult question: what to do with a damaged historic site in a residential neighbourhood. Options included:Demolishing the entire structure, including the facade, and selling the lot for private development.Rebuilding a new structure that mimicked the old school, at significant cost.Preserving the facade and converting the site into a public space that honoured the school’s legacy.City officials, neighbourhood residents and local historians leaned toward the third option. They saw an opportunity to turn a tragedy into a lasting community asset: a park that would keep the memory of the Ferry Street School alive while providing much-needed green space in the area.From charred shell to community parkIn 2023, fire gutted the Ferry Street School. Three years and $175,000 later, funded by city cash, grants, and neighbourhood donations, the lot reopened in August 2026 as Ferry Street Memorial Park.Rather than knocking everything down, workers saved the standing brick facade to anchor the property's history. They planted native trees, cleared walking paths, scattered benches, built play areas, and added history signs. Today, neighbours have a bright spot to catch up while kids run around. The space honours what used to be here, giving the local town a fresh place to gather without dwelling strictly on the past.Honouring history without recreating itOne of the most important decisions in the project was how to treat the remaining facade. Rather than trying to rebuild a replica school or hide the damage, the city chose to preserve the brick walls as they are, with visible signs of the fire’s impact. This approach keeps the site’s history legible to anyone who walks through the park. It also avoids the cost and complexity of reconstructing a full building. And, creates a unique memorial quality, where the facade acts as a monument rather than a functional structure. Interpretive panels and plaques provide context for visitors, explaining when the school was built, how it served the community and what happened in the 2023 fire.For older residents, the park is a place to share memories with children and grandchildren. For newer neighbours, it’s an introduction to the neighbourhood’s story.Why this park matters for the neighbourhoodFor many residents, Ferry Street Memorial Park fills a practical gap as well as an emotional one. The neighbourhood around the former school has limited public green space, and families often had to travel to other parts of Niles for parks and playgrounds.The new park offers: A safe, local place for children to play; a setting for informal gatherings, picnics and community events; and a visual and psychological break from streets and houses, improving the area’s overall livability.City officials also hope the park will spur additional investment in the neighbourhood, encouraging homeowners to improve properties and attracting small businesses that benefit from increased foot traffic.Community involvement from start to finishThe park’s creation was not just a top-down city project; it involved significant community input. Residents attended meetings, shared ideas about what they wanted in the park and helped prioritise features such as play equipment, seating and landscaping. Local organisations and donors contributed funds, materials and volunteer time.That broad involvement has given residents a sense of ownership over the park. It is not just a city asset; it is “their” park, born from a shared desire to make something positive out of a painful loss.New chapter: Ribbon-cuttingIn late August 2026, the city held a ribbon-cutting to officially open Ferry Street Memorial Park. Local officials, neighborhood residents and community group representatives came together to celebrate the project’s completion and to honor the history of the site. Speeches highlighted: The neighbourhood’s resilience in the midst of the fire. The significance of preserving local history in tangible ways. The value of public parks as places of connection, play and memory.For many attendees, the event felt like a turning point: the moment when a scar on the block became a source of pride.A model for other communitiesOther towns dealing with ruined landmarks can take a page from this playbook. Handling a damaged historic building isn’t an all-or-nothing choice between total demolition and a costly full rebuild. Saving just a key element, like an original facade, preserves local history at a fraction of the cost. Meanwhile, converting the rest of the site into a park serves both a practical everyday need and a commemorative one.This hybrid approach won’t fit every property, but when the circumstances line up, it turns a painful loss into lasting value.Looking aheadWith Ferry Street Memorial Park open, attention will turn to long-term care and programming. The city and community partners will need to: Maintain landscaping, paths and play features to keep the park safe and inviting. Consider holding occasional events like neighbourhood picnics or history remembrance gatherings. See how residents are using the park and make changes based on resident feedback. For a neighbourhood that lost its historic school to a devastating fire just three years ago, the park is a memorial and a promise that a community can rebuild after a devastating loss in a way that honours its past and serves its future.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Baltimore shopping centre opened in 1947 and declined for decades; 200 local residents became its co-owners, and 3 years later it has 10 new leases and a project expected to bring 100+ jobs
articles.summary: US News: A Baltimore shopping centre that once served as an important retail destination spent decades struggling with disinvestment and vacant storefronts. To.
articles.body: A Baltimore shopping centre that once served as an important retail destination spent decades struggling with disinvestment and vacant storefronts. Today, Edmondson Village Shopping Center is undergoing a different kind of transformation, driven partly by the people who live around it. According to the Kresge Foundation, the historic centre was acquired in 2023 with 200 community investors, giving local residents a direct ownership stake in the property. Three years later, 10 new leases have been signed, bringing services including groceries, primary care, child care and food retail. A planned headquarters for Meals on Wheels of Central Maryland is also expected to bring more than 100 jobs. The changes highlight how community ownership can become part of a broader effort to revive a neighbourhood shopping centre.From retail hub to declineEdmondson Village Shopping Center opened in 1947 as one of Baltimore's early major retail destinations. For decades, it served residents in the surrounding community, but the centre later faced years of decline. According to the Kresge Foundation, demographic shifts and disinvestment over roughly three decades contributed to the property's deterioration. Storefronts became vacant, reducing the range of goods and services available to local residents. The decline reflected broader changes in the neighbourhood and the difficulty of attracting investment to an older commercial centre.Residents become ownersA major change came in August 2023, when Chicago TREND acquired Edmondson Village Shopping Center through its Chicago TREND Real Estate Fund. The acquisition included 200 community investors, meaning local residents became stakeholders rather than simply customers. Chicago TREND is a certified benefit corporation that acquires and redevelops shopping centres while giving residents opportunities to invest in their neighbourhood commercial properties. Kresge Foundation invested $2 million in the Chicago TREND Real Estate Fund in 2022 through a program-related investment. The fund allows between 10% and 49% local resident ownership in each shopping-centre investment, with community investors able to participate with investments starting at $1,000. The model is intended to connect residents to the economic value created when a local property improves, allowing some of the benefits of redevelopment to remain within the community.Ten new leasesThree years after the acquisition, Edmondson Village is showing signs of renewed activity. Ten new leases have been signed, bringing services that residents had lacked. New tenants include a national grocery chain, a primary-care provider, child-care services and food retail. Physical improvements have also been made, including work on the roof, lighting, signage and site security. Construction for the new grocery store is also underway, adding another major service to the centre.More than 100 jobsThe redevelopment is expected to create employment as well as new services. Meals on Wheels of Central Maryland is in predevelopment on a planned 34,000-square-foot headquarters at the shopping centre. The project is expected to bring more than 100 jobs to the community. The headquarters would add an employment component to the retail and service activity returning to Edmondson Village.A community ownership modelThe Edmondson Village project is part of Chicago TREND's broader community-ownership approach. At Edmondson Village, the model gives residents a financial stake in a commercial property that had experienced years of decline. Their involvement is intended to connect them more directly to the centre's future and the economic activity generated by its redevelopment. The approach also changes the relationship between a shopping centre and the people who depend on it. Residents are not only customers of the businesses operating there; some are also owners with a stake in the property's success.A centre finding new lifeThe transformation of Edmondson Village is still underway, but the changes already mark a significant shift from the centre's long period of decline. For the 200 residents who became co-owners, the redevelopment represents more than new businesses and construction. It gives them a direct connection to the future of a commercial property in their own neighbourhood.The centre that opened in 1947 and later endured decades of disinvestment is now being reshaped through local ownership, new leases, physical improvements and planned job creation. Its revival offers an example of how community investment can play a role in bringing neighbourhood commercial spaces back to life.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Friday thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for congratulating her on becoming Italy’s longest continuousl.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Friday thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for congratulating her on becoming Italy’s longest continuously serving PM in the postwar period, saying the relationship between the two countries was “stronger than ever”.Sharing a post on X, Meloni said, “Thank you, dear Narendra Modi, for your words and for your friendship. The relationship between Italy and India is today stronger than ever.”“The Special Strategic Partnership that we launched during our last meeting is the recognition of the importance of this bond and of the will to unite the expertise of our Nations to create new opportunities for growth, seizing the extraordinary opportunities for collaboration that we have before us,” she said.“I am certain that Italy and India, together, will continue to strengthen the bond between our Continents as well, working side by side also to develop the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor,” she added.Meloni has served as Italy’s prime minister since October 22, 2022. On Thursday, after 1,413 consecutive days in office, she became the country’s longest continuously serving prime minister since World War II, surpassing the previous record held by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.Earlier in the day, PM Modi congratulated Meloni on the milestone, saying it reflected the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership.“Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership,” PM Modi said in a post on X.He said Meloni’s friendship had played an important role in strengthening the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership and that he looked forward to continuing close cooperation between the two countries.“My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead,” the PM added.The friendship between PM Modi and Meloni has often attracted attention on social media, with users referring to the duo as “Melodi”, a combination of their surnames.The trend began in November 2023 when Meloni shared a selfie with PM Modi from the COP28 summit in Dubai with the caption “Good friends at COP28 #Melodi.” The hashtag quickly became popular, generating memes and viral posts.The two leaders again drew attention at the G7 summit in June, when Meloni joked about their online popularity. During the traditional group photograph, she told PM Modi, “Yeah, we are the most famous couple on Instagram.”The “Melodi” buzz also resurfaced during PM Modi’s visit to Rome last month, when he presented Meloni with a packet of Parle’s Melody chocolates in a playful reference to the trend.PM Modi himself became India’s longest continuously serving elected prime minister on June 10, 2026, after completing 4,399 consecutive days in office.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2001, two Seattle Mariners raised an American flag after clinching their division days after 9/11; 25 years later, that moment has become a permanent stadium statue
articles.summary: US News: An iconic moment of national unity and sporting triumph after 9/11 has been turned into a permanent bronze statue at T-Mobile Park, as the Seattle Mar.
articles.body: An iconic moment of national unity and sporting triumph after 9/11 has been turned into a permanent bronze statue at T-Mobile Park, as the Seattle Mariners unveiled a monument showing two of their legendary players carrying the American flag around the field. The monument, located just inside the stadium’s centre-field gate as part of the team’s newly opened Legacy Plaza, shows former outfielders Mike Cameron and Mark McLemore running with the Stars and Stripes after the Mariners won the American League West division title on 19 September 2001. The ceremony was held on 3 September 2026, before the Mariners’ home game against the Oakland Athletics, according to FOX 13 Seattle, Yahoo Sports and KIRO 7 News. The unveiling came nearly 25 years after the event that inspired the statue.Cameron and McLemore both attended the dedication, along with legendary play-by-play announcer Rick Rizzs, who served as the master of ceremonies. "That was the first night that baseball was back," McLemore said during the ceremony, as reported by KIRO 7 News. "So, to be able to share that with the fans and the rest of the country…it really means a lot to me." "Those are the memories that are always with me. But, especially on a day like today, they're all flooding back," McLemore added. Cameron also spoke about what the honour meant to him. "For them to choose us. It's just special, man," Cameron said, as quoted by KIRO 7 News.Capturing a historic moment in Seattle sports historyThe statue captures the night in September 2001 when Major League Baseball returned after the 11 September terrorist attacks. That year, the Seattle Mariners had a historic season and eventually tied the Major League record with 116 regular-season wins. On the night they secured the division title, Cameron and McLemore made an unscripted lap around the ballpark while carrying the American flag. The moment became meaningful far beyond baseball during a time of national mourning. Both players were pleased with how accurately the bronze statue represented them. "They did it good, man. They got him to the tee," Cameron joked about his former teammate, as reported by KIRO 7 News. "He's still got his batting gloves in his back pocket." "I can't complain a bit," McLemore said. "Got my stirrups right. All of it. Everything." Rizzs also spoke about why the moment remains important. "The spirit of that moment lives where we're all standing right now," Rizzs said, as cited by KIRO 7 News.Interactive backdrop and youth baseball fundraising initiativeThe installation includes a detailed backdrop made up of 116 wooden baseball bats, with each bat representing one win from the historic 2001 season. More than 2,000 personalised commemorative baseball medallions have also been placed throughout the plaza around the statue. Season ticket holders and members of the public could buy customised bats for $1,000 and medallions for $250, allowing them to add their own messages, according to Seattle Sports and The Seattle Times. Money raised from the sale of the bats and medallions will go towards the Mariners Legacy Field Projects. The programme supports the restoration and upkeep of youth baseball and softball fields across Washington state.In statements released by the organisation and reported by Seattle Sports, Mariners chairman John Stanton explained the wider purpose of the project. "2001 was a momentous time for our community and for the Mariners," Stanton said. "The new Legacy Plaza reflects the deep connection between the Mariners and our community, commemorating one of the most meaningful moments in team history, while reinforcing our commitment to creating opportunities for youth across the Pacific Northwest." "The Legacy Plaza brings together our history, our fans and our commitment to the future of baseball and softball in our region," Stanton added. Cameron said supporting local sports facilities is especially important as the cost of youth sports continues to rise. "When I started playing, it was probably $10 or $20. And you paid for a hat, a belt, and some pants, and, obviously, you got your glove," Cameron said, as reported by KIRO 7 News. "But, now? It is so beyond that."Expanding stadium monuments at T-Mobile ParkThe 2001 flag statue is part of a larger effort by the Mariners to honour important players and moments from the team’s history. Earlier in 2026, the organisation unveiled a statue honouring Hall of Fame outfielder Ichiro Suzuki. Team officials have also confirmed that a statue dedicated to former Cy Young Award-winning pitcher Randy Johnson will be installed during the 2027 season, according to KIRO 7 News. The dedication came as the current 2026 Mariners team entered the final month of the regular season. The team is chasing a place in the postseason while remaining in the American League Wild Card race.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sri Lanka arrests ex-president Mahinda Rajapaksa’s son over Airbus deal
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Sri Lanka's main anti-graft agency on Friday arrested lawmaker Namal Rajapaksa, the son of former president Mahinda Rajapaksa, as part of a corruption.
articles.body: Sri Lanka's main anti-graft agency on Friday arrested lawmaker Namal Rajapaksa, the son of former president Mahinda Rajapaksa, as part of a corruption investigation into a controversial $2.3 billion Airbus aircraft deal.The Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) said the 40-year-old lawmaker was summoned for questioning over the 2013 transaction and arrested afterwards."The MP was arrested afterwards and will be taken before a magistrate," a commission official said.It was not immediately clear what charges Rajapaksa faces. His lawyer, Nishantha Dayananda, confirmed the arrest.The investigation centres on allegations that Airbus agreed to channel part of the proceeds from the purchase as bribes to senior Sri Lankan officials and politicians. The deal involved the purchase of 10 Airbus aircraft and required cabinet approval during Mahinda Rajapaksa's presidency from 2005 to 2015.CIABOC also questioned the former president in May over allegations that he received kickbacks linked to the aircraft purchase.The Rajapaksa family has denied receiving bribes and has dismissed corruption allegations against them as politically motivated.Former SriLankan Airlines chief executive Kapila Chandrasena told investigators in March that he had handed nearly $500,000 in kickbacks to Namal Rajapaksa.According to court submissions, Chandrasena initially told investigators that he had paid Rajapaksa 60 million Sri Lankan rupees, equivalent to $461,000 at the time, in three instalments in 2013. He later retracted the statement, saying it had been made under pressure.Chandrasena was found dead at a relative's home in May, shortly before he was due to be rearrested. The cause of his death has not been established.A previous joint investigation by US, British and French authorities found that Airbus had agreed to pay about $16 million in bribes in Sri Lanka, with $1.7 million allegedly routed to Chandrasena before the scandal came to light.The Airbus deal was eventually cancelled by a new Sri Lankan government in 2016.SriLankan Airlines, the country's debt-laden flag carrier, has accumulated losses estimated at nearly $2 billion, while repeated efforts to privatise the airline have failed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Vice President JD Vance was surprised to be asked about his weight-loss secret at an official White House press briefing but chuckled, saying it only meant he used to be very fat. "So, when you're the vice president of the United States and one of the first questions at a press conference in the White House is how much weight you've lost, you must have gotten very fat," Vance jokingly responded.Vance did not gatekeep the weight loss secret and revealed that the credit goes to RFK Jr's sauerkraut (fermented cabbage). "I was talking to my wife on Fat Tuesday, Mardi Gras, and I was like, 'I think I'm going to give up sugar,'" Vance told Fox News Channel's Senior White House Correspondent Peter Doocy who asked the weightloss question.Vance said he called Bobby Kennedy, since he's "really into health," and told him he's thinking about giving up sugar. "And Bobby Kennedy says, 'No, no, no, no. I've got something that's way better than that and way more intense,'" Vance said. "Basically I eat a lot of high-protein stuff, and I eat a lot of sauerkraut. And let's just say that if that was Fat Tuesday, Fat Wednesday never came."Call BobbyJD Vance's weight loss secret is: "if you want to lose weight, call Bobby Kennedy. And if you want to enjoy what you eat, do not call Bobby Kennedy."Weight loss before presidential runOn Fox & Friends, host Brian Kilmeade offered his own theory about the vice president's transformation, saying Vance was “losing weight because he's gonna run for president -- just like everyone else.”Vance has not declared that he will seek the Republican presidential nomination in 2028. However, he is widely viewed as one of the potential contenders who could emerge as the party's next presidential standard-bearer after President Donald Trump.The vice president has acknowledged that a potential 2028 campaign is something he will eventually have to consider. In a June interview with CBS, he said he had not made a decision and suggested that he and his wife, Usha Vance, would discuss the future of their family after the 2026 midterm elections. Usha Vance has also indicated that she is keeping an open mind about what could come next for her husband's political career.What is sauerkraut?Sauerkraut is finely shredded raw cabbage that has been preserved and flavored through lactic acid fermentation using salt. RFK Jr spoke highly of sauerkraut and is believed to have converted Trump's entire cabinet to his diet that consists of sauerkraut and meat. Kennedy Jr travels with his cooler of sauerkraut jars when he travels. articles.title: Russia's 'Web' system: New defence for energy and oil infrastructure against drones
articles.summary: International News: Russian companies have developed a modular metal structure designed to protect oil storage facilities, electrical substations and other critical infra.
articles.body: Russian companies have developed a modular metal structure designed to protect oil storage facilities, electrical substations and other critical infrastructure from drone attacks, as Ukrainian strikes continue to target Russia’s energy sector.Called “Web”, the system was developed by RT-Project Technologies, a subsidiary of state-owned defence and technology conglomerate Rostec, in partnership with Standard-Elektrik. The system was presented at a closed event in Tver.According to the developers, the basic version of the structure can withstand a direct impact from a drone weighing up to 200 kg and travelling at up to 250 kmph. The system can be installed around facilities more than 25 metres high and expanded to cover areas of virtually any size.The structure has completed field tests for seismic stability, while testing its ability to withstand strikes from different types of drones is still underway. It is currently undergoing trial operations at several fuel and energy facilities.The protective system consists of load-bearing columns, a network of power cables and supports. It uses bolted joints rather than welding, allowing installation in confined spaces and locations with heightened fire risks. The developers say this can reduce installation costs while making deployment faster and safer.The metal components are also treated with factory-applied hot-dip galvanizing to protect them against corrosion.The development comes as Ukrainian drones have repeatedly targeted Russian oil refineries, fuel depots and other energy infrastructure, with strikes causing fires and disrupting operations at some facilities.In June, Russian President Vladimir Putin acknowledged that repeated Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries had contributed to fuel shortages.The new system also comes amid growing concern over the security of Russia’s energy infrastructure. Earlier this year, hackers gained access to a confidential Rosneft project concerning measures to protect the company's facilities from Ukrainian drone attacks.

articles.title: In 1969, Malcolm Forbes bought Colorado's Trinchera Ranch; 35 years later his family permanently protected 80,000 acres, the largest donated conservation easement in state history
articles.summary: US News: A huge area of alpine wilderness in southern Colorado has been permanently protected from commercial development after the family of late publishing t.
articles.body: A huge area of alpine wilderness in southern Colorado has been permanently protected from commercial development after the family of late publishing tycoon Malcolm Forbes donated an 80,000-acre conservation easement. The agreement, managed by Colorado Open Lands, is the largest donated conservation easement in Colorado’s history. It permanently limits subdivision and commercial development on the historic Trinchera Ranch, protecting large areas of pine forests, mountain peaks and important wildlife habitats in the Sangre de Cristo mountain range. The landmark agreement completes 35 years of stewardship by the Forbes family, which first bought the historic property in 1969. Through the easement, the family ensured that the mountain landscape would remain in its natural state forever, regardless of future changes in ownership. Documents published by Colorado Open Lands and the National Park Service highlight the environmental importance of the agreement. The protected land connects large high-altitude areas that provide important habitats for native elk, black bears, bighorn sheep and cutthroat trout.High-altitude wilderness and historic rootsLocated in Costilla County in Colorado’s San Luis Valley, Trinchera Ranch is part of the historic 1841 Sangre de Cristo Land Grant. The original grant covered hundreds of thousands of acres across southern Colorado and northern New Mexico before being divided into separate agricultural and timber properties over the following century. Publishing tycoon Malcolm Forbes bought Trinchera Ranch and the nearby Blanca Ranch in 1969 for about $50 per acre. In 1971, Forbes separated a 66,000-acre section along the western boundary to create the Sangre de Cristo Ranches residential subdivision. He kept more than 110,000 acres for ranching, timber management and personal recreation. After Forbes died in 1990, his children looked at long-term conservation options to stop the remaining wilderness from being divided into smaller residential lots or commercial developments. The resulting 80,000-acre easement donated to Colorado Open Lands legally binds both current and future owners. It prevents subdivision while allowing traditional farming and forestry activities to continue under strict environmental rules.Protecting alpine ecosystems and wildlife corridorsEnvironmental groups and state conservation officials have praised the easement as an important protection for the San Luis Valley’s natural environment. The protected land includes peaks rising above 14,000 feet, including areas near Mount Blanca, as well as miles of untouched alpine streams that flow into the Rio Grande basin. According to reports from Colorado Open Lands, protecting private land on this scale is important for maintaining wildlife migration routes. Large private ranches across the American West often face financial pressure to divide their land into smaller properties or holiday home developments, which can break up sensitive ecosystems. By protecting 80,000 connected acres through a permanent conservation easement, the Forbes family created a protected buffer next to public lands, including the Rio Grande National Forest and nearby federal wildlife preserves. A conservation easement allows the land to remain privately owned and managed while permanently giving up the right to build high-density housing, industrial facilities or major commercial infrastructure.Transition to new ownership under Louis BaconThe conservation plan created by the Forbes family later helped establish wider environmental protections across the ranch complex. In November 2007, three years after the original 80,000-acre easement was completed, the Forbes estate sold the entire 171,400-acre property, including Trinchera Ranch and Blanca Ranch, to financier and conservationist Louis Bacon for $175 million, according to Wikipedia and local real estate archives. Bacon built on the Forbes family’s conservation efforts by placing the remaining unprotected land under additional conservation agreements. In 2012, Bacon worked with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and Colorado Open Lands to donate more easements, helping establish the Sangre de Cristo Conservation Area. Today, the entire original 172,000-acre estate is protected from future subdivision, creating one of the largest connected private conservation areas in North America. The Forbes family’s original 80,000-acre donation remains the foundation of the wider regional conservation effort. Trinchera Ranch continues to operate as a working timber and eco-tourism ranch, showing how private landownership and long-term environmental protection can exist together in the American West.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bargaining tactics? Why BJP's 'solo pitch' in Punjab may have message for Akalis
articles.summary: India News: Is the BJP playing hardball with the Akalis in Punjab? Yet another senior BJP leader has announced that the party will contest all 117 assembly seats .
articles.body: Is the BJP playing hardball with the Akalis in Punjab? Yet another senior BJP leader has announced that the party will contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab on its own strength.BJP national general secretary Satish Poonia, in his first media interaction after being appointed the party's organisational in-charge for Punjab, made it clear that the message from the central leadership was to prepare for all 117 constituencies in the state. He also sought to play down Shiromani Akali Dal chief Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi last month, saying meetings between political leaders should not automatically be read as signs of an alliance.Poonia is not the first senior BJP leader to reiterate the 'solo contest' point.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh had earlier told party functionaries in Punjab that the BJP would contest all 117 assembly seats independently.And yet, the speculation of an alliance between the two parties refuses to go away.The question then is whether the BJP is really shutting the door on its old ally or raising the bar before any possible deal.BJP's message: We can do it aloneThe BJP today has reasons to sound more confident than it did when both parties went their separate ways.The BJP in Punjab was the junior partner of the Akalis for decades. The arrangement gave the BJP a share of Punjab's urban and Hindu-dominated constituencies while the SAD remained the dominant force in the alliance.In the 2017 assembly election, the last Punjab polls the two parties contested together, the SAD fought 94 seats and the BJP just 23. The BJP won three and the Akalis 15.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();This arrangement will clearly no longer work for the BJP.Since splitting with the Akalis, the BJP has been working towards a plan. The party has been trying to expand beyond its old pockets in Punjab, in line with its national growth, and build an independent base. The West Bengal victory has indeed strengthened the confidence within the party. Punjab BJP leaders have also publicly argued that the party's improved vote share and national presence have strengthened the case for fighting the elections independently.That makes the repeated declaration of contesting 117 seats more than just a message to the Akalis. It is also a message to BJP workers that the party intends to build its own organisation across Punjab.But the doors don't seem completely shutInterestingly, even in the middle of this high-pitched rhetoric, the Student Organisation of India (SOI), which is the students’ wing of the Shiromani Akali Dal, extended support to the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) candidate in the Panjab University Campus Students’ Council elections and helped its candidate win the presidential post.The SOI offered this olive branch to BJP’s student wing a day before the voting and helped ABVP create a record of winning the top post in the students’ council election for the second time in a row.This campus politics bonhomie was significant messaging. The Akalis, who had walked away from the decades-old alliance with the BJP in 2020 over the now-repealed farm bills, have dropped very clear and open hints that they desperately want to revive the ties.There have been a series of overtures from their end to seek an alliance without expressing that in as many words.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Akalis have not been subtle about wanting alliance with BJPIf the BJP is keeping its cards close to its chest, the Akalis have been far more open about it.The PM Modi-Sukhbir Badal meeting was perhaps the beginning of this outreach. It was their first one-on-one political meeting since the SAD walked out of the BJP-led NDA in 2020 over the three farm laws, ending an alliance that had lasted nearly two decades.Days after this meeting, the SAD reversed its stand on the Delimitation Bill and announced its support for the constitutional amendment bill which the BJP is trying to pass in Parliament. This was a huge U-turn that prompted digs from the ruling AAP and the Congress over the SAD’s desperation for an alliance with the BJP.The shift in stance drew attention because the party had earlier taken a much more critical position on delimitation. The SAD had in April stated in Lok Sabha that the BJP was repeatedly changing the goal post on women's reservation and decried that the delimitation exercise was being conducted in the garb of the Women's Reservation Bill.Then came more signals from within the Akali leadership.Senior Akali leader Bikram Singh Majithia went public advocating an alliance, and said that people want SAD and the BJP to come together for peace, development and progress of Punjab.Majithia's statement came after his sister and former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal stoked fresh speculation about a re-alliance between the Akali Dal and the BJP by expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that carried progress to Punjab from Delhi.None of these statements amounted to a formal alliance proposal. However, they made it clear that the Akali leadership was increasingly interested in reviving ties with the BJP.Akalis need BJP more than beforeThe reason is not difficult to see. The Akalis have been pushed to the fringes of Punjab politics.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Its vote share and seat share have declined in the last few elections. In fact, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP managed a huge lead over SAD in terms of vote share.The BJP secured 18.56% of the votes but failed to win a parliamentary seat in Punjab. The Akali Dal, despite winning Bathinda, finished with 13.42% vote share.The BJP also finished ahead of SAD candidates across several constituencies and led in 24 assembly segments. In the 2022 assembly polls, by comparison, the BJP's vote share was only around 6.6%, while SAD was a little over 18%.That perhaps explains why the Akalis seem desperate for an alliance. Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has claimed that the Shiromani Akali Dal leadership is "on its knees" to forge an alliance with the BJP and return to power in the state to "loot" it again.So, the big question is: why is the BJP acting tough? Is it against reviving the alliance with the Akalis? Or is the BJP just playing hardball to ensure that it is the “big brother” in any future alliance?For the Akalis, the decline has been much more painful.Akalis, who dominated Punjab politics for years, were reduced to three seats in the 2022 assembly election and one Lok Sabha seat in 2024. Now, the party has to compete not only with the Congress but also with AAP, which swept the last state election, and also a BJP trying to expand independently.That perhaps explains the urgency.Why BJP may have kept the door openWhen BJP and SAD were in alliance earlier, there was little ambiguity about who was the senior partner.The SAD had more seats and more say in deciding the assembly seats and the chief ministerial candidate. The BJP accepted most terms because the arrangement perhaps gave the BJP a space where its independent visibility was limited.But now, if there is an alliance between the two again, it surely will be on completely different terms.The BJP has spent the years since the split trying to build an identity of its own in Punjab. It has brought leaders from other parties into its fold, expanded its organisation and fielded candidates across the entire state in the 2024 Lok Sabha election.Even in recent weeks, it has continued inducting figures from outside the party as it prepares for the assembly contest.For the BJP, therefore, returning to an arrangement in which it simply receives around 20-odd seats would be difficult. This is perhaps where the bargaining may be happening. Therefore, the real question might just be if the Akalis are willing to accept the changed political reality.There is another reason why the BJP may be keeping the Akalis guessing.Declaring an alliance too early could derail BJP's bid to strengthen its organisation in the state build an independent identity. Keeping the 117-seat option alive allows the BJP to continue expanding and encouraging its cadres.The BJP knows the Akalis are willing to return. There is little reason for the BJP to make any commitment before discussing seats and leadership.The public posturing notwithstanding, the BJP also stands to gain from a possible alliance. The BJP's 18.56% vote share in the Lok Sabha election did not translate into a single seat. This shows that the party did expand its base, but that vote share by itself may not be enough.The Akalis, meanwhile, still have traditional pockets of support. That gives both sides something the other may want.But does BJP actually need the Akalis?Fighting independently gives it the freedom to contest every region, develop new leaders and try to move beyond its traditional urban base. Even an election in which it improves substantially without forming the government could further that objective. An alliance with SAD could interrupt that process.Also, the Sikh community's identity continues to play an important role in Punjab politics. For the BJP, a renewed alliance with the Akali Dal could help it reach sections of Sikh voters and rural Punjab where the party has traditionally struggled to build a strong independent base.For now, the two sides appear to be speaking in very different registers.The Akalis have repeatedly sent signals that they are willing to reopen the relationship. The BJP is listening but not reacting. For now, all BJP leaders are maintaining that the party is preparing for all 117 seats.Yet the Modi-Sukhbir meeting, the SOI-ABVP cooperation and reports of discussions behind the scenes mean the possibility of an alliance cannot be written off either.It is possible that the BJP means exactly what it says and will go into the election alone. But if the two former allies do eventually come together, it is unlikely to be a return to the partnership that existed before 2020.The fight, therefore, may not just be about whether BJP and SAD become allies again. It may be about who gets to be the 'big brother' this time.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1928, Henry Ford tried to revolutionise coal mining in a remote West Virginia town; 70 years later the abandoned mine became a national park site
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Hidden deep in a West Virginia gorge is an abandoned coal town with a surprising connection to Henry Ford. Nuttallburg was once a thriving mining comm.
articles.body: Hidden deep in a West Virginia gorge is an abandoned coal town with a surprising connection to Henry Ford. Nuttallburg was once a thriving mining community, its fortunes built on the rich coal and the railway that carried the fuel to distant customers. For decades, miners, railway workers and their families helped turn the isolated settlement into a busy industrial centre. Then Ford arrived. In the 1920s, his company took control of the mines as part of an ambitious attempt to secure the raw materials needed for his expanding industrial operations.But the plan exposed an unexpected weakness: owning the mine did not mean controlling the railway that transported its coal. Ford eventually sold his interests in 1928. Mining continued until 1958, after which Nuttallburg slowly disappeared beneath vegetation. Today, its surviving tipple, foundations and roads offer a rare glimpse into a coal town that once played a small but fascinating role in Ford’s industrial empire.How Nuttallburg turned a remote gorge into a thriving mining communityNuttallburg began taking shape in the late 19th century, when the demand for coal was transforming the New River Gorge. According to the National Park Service, in 1870, John Nuttall, an English-born entrepreneur, recognised the potential of the coal seams around Keeneys Creek and began acquiring land and developing the infrastructure needed to extract and move the fuel.The Chesapeake and Ohio Railway reached the gorge in 1873, providing something the isolated mining settlements badly needed: a way to get coal out.Nuttallburg grew alongside the railway. Coal mined high above the river was brought down towards the processing works, prepared for shipment and then loaded onto trains. The coal from the New River region was prized for its low smoke, making it attractive to industrial customers far beyond West Virginia.By the turn of the 20th century, Nuttallburg was no longer simply a collection of mine workings. It had become a functioning community, with workers and families living around an industry that dominated nearly every part of daily life.John Nuttall died in 1897, but the operation continued under his heirs. For decades, the settlement remained connected to the fortunes of the coal trade. Then came Henry Ford.How Ford brought Nuttallburg into his visionDuring the 1920s, Ford was pursuing a business strategy that went beyond making cars. He wanted greater control over the materials and processes feeding his industrial operations, a concept known as vertical integration.Coal was important to that system. It was needed for industrial production, including the steelmaking operations supplying Ford's factories. Nuttallburg caught Ford's attention.His company leased the town's mines and took control of the operation during the 1920s. Under the Fordson Coal Company, the site received investment and changes intended to make the mining complex more efficient. The old operation was being reshaped to fit a much larger industrial vision.For a remote settlement tucked into a narrow gorge, the connection was unusual. Ford's name was associated with mass production, motor cars and enormous factories. Nuttallburg, by contrast, was reached by a steep road and surrounded by rugged Appalachian terrain.Yet the mine fitted into Ford's plans because of what lay underground.How Nuttallburg showed the limits of Ford’s industrial empireThe strategy ran into a basic difficulty. Mining the coal was only part of the job. It still had to be transported to the places where Ford needed it.The railway remained essential. Ford could lease and improve the mine, but he could not gain the same control over the railway that carried the coal away. That weakened the logic behind his attempt to bring the different stages of production under one roof, or at least under one corporate structure.According to the National Park Service, after about eight years, Ford's involvement with Nuttallburg came to an end. He sold his interests in the mines in 1928, bringing the chapter of Ford's direct association with the operation to a close.It was an important lesson in the limits of industrial control. Owning or managing a mine did not mean controlling the network that connected it to the wider economy.How the end of coal mining transformed Nuttallburg foreverNuttallburg did not shut down when Ford left. The mine passed through three owners, although its importance gradually diminished as the market for New River coal changed. In its later years, production was increasingly directed towards local needs rather than the distant industrial markets that had helped make the settlement prosperous.The decline was slow rather than sudden. Mines could remain active long after their most prosperous period had passed, especially in communities where coal was the main source of employment.At Nuttallburg, commercial mining finally stopped in 1958.The change was profound. A settlement that had once depended on miners, railway workers and the movement of coal was left without the industry that had created it. Houses disappeared, buildings deteriorated and vegetation began reclaiming parts of the site.What had been an industrial workplace was gradually becoming an archaeological landscape.What Nuttallburg’s surviving buildings reveal about its industrial pastThe most striking survivor is the coal tipple, the large structure used in handling and loading coal. It stands above the old railway alignment, giving an idea of the scale of the operation that once occupied the valley.Other remnants are scattered through the site. Foundations, industrial structures, old roads and traces of the settlement remain, although some are easier to recognise than others.The surrounding landscape has become part of the story. Trees and vines now grow around structures that were once maintained because they were essential to production. In places, the boundary between the industrial remains and the forest is difficult to distinguish.Seventy years later, Nuttallburg changed handsThe Ford era was long over by the time the Nuttall family made a decision that would shape the site's future.In 1998, ownership of Nuttallburg was transferred to the National Park Service. The timing came four decades after mining had ended and roughly 70 years after Ford's involvement with the operation. The site was subsequently documented and assessed for its historical significance. In 2005, Nuttallburg was added to the National Register of Historic Places.Preservation work followed. Vegetation that had obscured parts of the old complex was cleared, while surviving structures were stabilised. By 2011, the National Park Service had completed a multi-year effort aimed at making the remains safer to study and protecting what was left.The result is now regarded as one of West Virginia's most intact historic coal-mining complexes and one of the country's more complete surviving industrial coal sites.How visitors reach historic NuttallburgNuttallburg is not a place reached by an easy drive through a modern tourist district. The route itself reflects the geography that shaped the settlement.Keeneys Creek Road is narrow, winding and steep, with a mixture of paved and gravel sections. Much of it is only wide enough for one vehicle. Passing another car can mean finding a suitable pull-off, and in some sections there is little room to do so. Large vehicles and trailers are therefore discouraged.The main parking area lies beyond the former community, with accessible parking a little farther along, closer to the tipple.Visitors also pass through what was once Nuttallburg's African American community on the approach. Interpretive panels along the road provide information about the people and places that formed part of the settlement's history, rather than focusing solely on the machinery and mine workings.There is another way in for those approaching from the direction of Lansing. A trail from Beauty Mountain Road leads towards the headhouse area. It follows an old administrative road for roughly three-quarters of a mile, but the route is steep and strenuous.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security service in central Kyiv on Friday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said, as Russian drone attacks on the capital continued for a 10th consecutive day.At least seven people were injured in the attack, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Heavy black smoke rose over the city centre following the strike, while emergency services and ambulances rushed to the scene near the historic Saint Sophia Cathedral."The drone was aimed directly at the office of the Head of the Security Service in that building," Zelenskiy said on the Telegram app.Zelenskiy said he had ordered a response to the strike, including an attack mirroring the Russian assault where possible.He ordered "an appropriate, tangible response and, where possible, one that mirrors this ⁠strike, to the Russians once everything was ready."It was not immediately clear whether any SBU personnel were among those injured.The strike marks a rare instance of a Ukrainian government building being damaged during more than four-and-a-half years of war with Russia. The SBU plays a key role in Ukraine's war effort and has carried out high-impact operations targeting Russia's military and energy infrastructure.The attack also damaged a building opposite the SBU headquarters, according to the owner of the Zavertailo bakery, who said the premises were destroyed.Kyiv has faced repeated Russian drone attacks for 10 consecutive days. A university in the city centre was also struck on Wednesday.The latest attack came as the SBU continues operations against Russian targets. The agency has been involved in major operations including the 2022 bombing of a bridge linking Russia with occupied Crimea and the 2025 Spiderweb drone attack on Russian strategic bombers.Russia has also accused Ukraine of carrying out covert attacks and has denounced the killing of Russian military and other officials attributed to Ukrainian operations as terrorist attacks.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Tesla Cybercabs are under federal investigation a day after Austin launch
articles.summary: The vehicles have no steering wheels or pedals, which appears to be central to the NHTSA probe.
articles.body:
Federal transportation officials have opened an investigation into Tesla's self-driving taxis, hours after the automaker held a launch event for the Cybercab in Austin. The vehicles have no pedals or steering wheels, which appears to be at the center of the probe by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

TechCrunch was first to report the NHTSA investigation.

In a brief summarizing the audit query it is conducting, the NHTSA notes that Tesla had "notified the Agency that it certified those Cybercab vehicles as compliant with all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards (FMVSS)." Under federal law, automakers are allowed to self-certify that their vehicles meet safety regulations. Those regulations, however, require cars to have steering wheels and brakes.

The NHTSA wants to know if Tesla's self-certification of the Cybercab "depended on determinations that certain F.M.V.S.S. are inapplicable to the Cybercab," meaning that the company may have decided some of the regulations did not apply to the self-driving taxis.

Tesla launched its Cybercabs at a glitzy invitation-only event in Austin on Thursday night, where it invited influencers to take test rides in the vehicles. The company teased the event on its social media, with a post to X two hours before the launch that said "the future has arrived in Austin," and a voice-over from CEO Elon Musk describing the Cybercab as "the first vehicle specifically built for unsupervised full self-driving."

The company first revealed a prototype for the Cybercab in 2024 at an event on a Hollywood soundstage. Tesla has registered 45 Cybercabs as part of its robotaxi fleet in Texas, but has said rides in Cybercabs will only be available in a limited section of Austin. The company began robotaxi service in Austin last year, using modified versions of its Model Y.

Tesla did not reply to a request for comment on Friday. The company's stock was down more than 5% in early trading.

articles.title: Trump to fly Qatari-gifted Boeing 747 for international trips despite security concerns
articles.summary: US News: President Trump will commence international travel on a Qatari-gifted Boeing 747, raising security issues following intelligence threats. Upgrades for better security are planned but details remain undisclosed.
articles.body: President Donald Trump is set to use the Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar for his trip to Ireland next week, a senior White House official told The Washington Post.The flight will be Trump’s first international trip on the aircraft since he was secretly transferred to another US military plane during his return from Turkey in July after US officials received intelligence about a possible Iranian threat.Trump has used the Qatari aircraft for domestic travel since early July. But the plane reportedly lacks some of the security features installed on the heavily modified aircraft traditionally used as Air Force One.Trump said in July that the aircraft would be sent for additional work and “maxed out”. The administration has not said when the upgrades will begin or how long they will take.The White House has also not disclosed the expected cost. The US government has already spent about $400 million modifying the aircraft.A senior administration official told The Post that the government maintains security measures to ensure the safety and reliability of the presidential aircraft, while declining to discuss specific upgrades or modifications.The decision comes as Trump prepares for increased travel ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. He is expected to visit Texas next week for a Republican event and has said he plans to travel to Alaska and other states with competitive races, the newspaper reported.Security concerns surrounding the aircraft intensified after Trump’s July trip to Turkey for the NATO summit. He did not use the Qatari jet for his return to Britain after officials received intelligence about a possible Iranian attack.Trump initially said he had left Turkey aboard the former Air Force One. The Post later reported that he was moved from the older presidential aircraft to an Air Force C-32A, which flew him to Britain.The older Air Force One remained in Turkey as a decoy. Trump travelled on the C-32A with a small group that included Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, while other officials and journalists were unaware of the switch.Qatar’s aircraft was offered as an interim option while the United States waited for replacement presidential planes. Boeing received a contract in 2017 to build two new 747s, but it is unclear whether they will be ready before Trump’s term ends in January 2029.The Government Accountability Office has estimated that the replacement programme will cost more than $5.6 billion. The figure has prompted lawmakers to question the cost and security of the government-owned aircraft compared with the Qatari jet.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Bunkfest: Free festival returns after last minute train scare
articles.summary: Bunkfest takes place on the banks of the River Thames in Wallingford between Friday and Sunday.
articles.body:
A free music festival is taking place after a last minute scare threw this year's edition into doubt.

Bunkfest is a community festival on the banks of the River Thames in Wallingford, Oxfordshire, that takes place from Friday to Sunday filling the town with live music, dancing and other entertainment.

The event is organised by volunteers, and gets its name from the Bunk Railway line which runs between the south Oxfordshire town and nearby Cholsey.

A crash on the historic railway in August damaged equipment on a level crossing, with all trains cancelled and Bunkfest thrown into doubt. But repairs carried out by Network Rail over the bank holiday weekend resolved the problems.

The rail line is used by festival organisers to prevent as many people as possible from travelling in cars instead using the much larger Cholsey Station to get people into Wallingford.

Bunkfest chairman Michael Palfrey told the BBC there "was a little bit of doubt" over whether the event would be able to take place.

"We were given a date [for repairs] a couple of weeks ago and they [Network Rail] did manage to stick to it and get the job done," he said.

"Finally, we've managed to get it over the line."

The shuttle trains over the weekend between Cholsey and Wallingford make up Bunkfest Fringe - with entertainers onboard and also at both stations.

Tickets for the trains must be purchased, but the rest of the weekend's entertainment in Wallingford is free.

That includes on Saturday, when English rhythm and blues band Dr Feelgood will headline.

Frontman Robert Kane said he was "really looking forward" to performing at the festival on the Thames.

"We hit the stage at 100mph and keep that going for an hour and a half," he said of the band's performance style.

"There is no let up, so if anybody's up for that, get yourself down to Bunkfest."

"I've had a look at the bill and there's also a fantastic range of acts on around us," he said.

articles.title: Judge plans to declare mistrial in Lindsay Clancy murder trial after jury fails to reach a verdict
articles.summary: The jury was unable to come to an agreement on whether Clancy was criminally responsible for killing her three children after more than 38 hours of deliberat...
articles.body:
The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial announced his intention to declare a mistrial on Friday after the jury was unable to reach a verdict on whether the former nurse, whose defense argued that postpartum psychosis caused her to kill her young children, bears criminal responsibility for her actions. Clancy's attorney was given one hour to petition a higher court to stay that decision before it becomes final.

Clancy, 36, admitted to strangling her children — Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and 8-month-old Callan — at their Duxbury, Mass., home in January 2023. However, her lawyers argued that she could not be held criminally responsible because she was suffering from a rare mental illness that they said made her unable to understand the wrongfulness of her actions.

Prosecutors contended that Clancy, who was never formally diagnosed with postpartum psychosis, carefully planned the killings and bears full responsibility for her children's deaths.

The trial hinged largely on discussions of Clancy's mental state. Over nearly five weeks of testimony, a series of family members and medical professionals took the stand to describe the mental and emotional struggles she endured in the months leading up to the killings.

In the end, the jury was unable to come to a consensus on whether Clancy was criminally responsible, resulting in a mistrial. She had been charged with three counts of murder in the first degree. The case finally ended following more than 38 hours of deliberation after the jury came to the judge for a third time to inform him that they were deadlocked, which triggered an automatic mistrial under Massachusetts law.

It wasn't immediately clear after the ruling whether the prosecution would seek a retrial or whether Clancy would remain in custody while the next steps in her case are determined.

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse, had been receiving treatment for severe mental health issues in the months after the birth of her third child, including intrusive thoughts, depression and insomnia. Her ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, testified that she was "having one of her best days" in the hours before she killed her children on Jan. 24, 2023. She had taken their daughter to a doctor's appointment, built a snowman with their kids and helped with art projects, he said.

"I was hopeful," Patrick told the jury. "She seemed much better."

Later that evening, however, Patrick came home from running errands to find that Lindsay had strangled their three children with exercise bands and attempted to end her own life by cutting herself and jumping out of a second-story window. Lindsay suffered a spinal cord injury from the fall that left her paralyzed from the waist down.

According to legal filings , Lindsay had described hearing "a loud, demanding, repetitious" male voice telling her, "This is your last chance. Kill the children so you can kill yourself," and said she "felt a force come over her."

"I lost all control. My body started acting without any control on my part. I was just following commands," she said afterward, according to a lawsuit she filed this year that accuses the medical providers who treated her in the months before the killings of negligence and malpractice.

The course of Lindsay's mental health decline was a central topic throughout the trial. She had reported experiencing postpartum anxiety after the births of her first two children. Those symptoms, along with signs of depression, returned in a more pronounced way after her youngest child, Callan, was born in May 2022.

Her anxiety escalated after roughly 12 weeks postpartum , around the time when she was scheduled to end her maternity leave and return to work.

In September 2022, Lindsay began seeking treatment for her symptoms. Over the next four months, she received care from several psychiatric professionals and was prescribed a total of 13 medications , including Zoloft, Ativan, Prozac and Ambien. Despite this treatment, her mental health continued to decline.

"She could not emote. She couldn't feel love. She couldn't feel happiness. She felt heavy. She couldn't walk. She couldn't bathe. She had difficulty relating to people," Lindsay's attorney, Kevin Reddington, said while describing her condition during the trial.

In mid-November, she went to the emergency room for help with her increasingly severe insomnia, but the treatment she received did not work. By the end of that month, she reported experiencing symptoms of dissociation that left her unable to determine what was real.

"She had horrible thoughts," Dr. Paul Zeizel, a clinical and forensic psychologist who spoke with Lindsay after the killings, testified. "She felt that people could actually hear her thoughts. The thoughts were so loud that strangers could hear them."

In her personal diary, which was read as evidence during the trial, Lindsay described living with "crazy brain fog" and feeling "incredibly sad and guilty" about not breastfeeding Callum.

Lindsay's mental health continued to deteriorate throughout December as she experienced suicidal ideations and, according to her lawsuit, "auditory" hallucinations. Her mother, Paula Musgrove, testified that toward the end of the month, Lindsay told her and her husband that she had "thoughts of harming the children."

Patrick's mother, Susan Clancy, testified at the trial that Lindsay was "begging for help" in the weeks before the killings.

Lindsay checked herself into a psychiatric hospital on New Year's Day and stayed there for five days before being discharged on Jan. 5, 2023. According to her phone's search data , which was presented at trial, she searched online for information on suicide methods and treating hallucinations, and sought answers to the question, "Can you treat a sociopath?"

She had a final virtual appointment with a psychiatrist on Jan. 23, the day before the killings.

Prosecutors refute Lindsay Clancy's claims

Throughout the trial, prosecutors argued that, although Lindsay was clearly struggling with her mental health, she acted "intentionally, rationally and swiftly" when she made the choice to kill her children.

"This was not a woman in the throes of psychosis," Shanan Buckingham, an assistant district attorney for Plymouth County, told the jury during her opening statement in late July.

The prosecution relied heavily on the testimony of medical professionals who treated Lindsay, each of whom said she did not exhibit signs of the kind of psychotic break that she says led her to commit the killings.

"I did not have any concerns about her safety or her risk for anybody else," said Dr. Alia Goodheart, a psychiatrist who led Lindsay's care during her inpatient hospital stay in early January.

Dr. Jennifer Tufts, a psychiatrist who treated Lindsay from September 2022 until the day before the killings, told the jury that Lindsay never expressed specific intentions to take her own life and never mentioned thoughts of harming her children. Prosecutors say she hid those thoughts.

"I would have been very concerned if I had heard that," Tufts said.

Psychiatric nurse practitioner Rebecca Jollotta testified that Lindsay told her about "persistent, intrusive thoughts of suicide" but had not discussed a specific plan to hurt herself or her children. Jollotta also said Lindsay showed no signs of psychosis or mania.

Goodheart, Tufts and Jollotta are among the medical professionals and clinics that are named in Lindsay's lawsuit alleging they "failed her completely" when she was in severe need of help.

"This is a woman that did not get … the medical treatment that she so deserved," Reddington said during his opening statement to the jury.

Lindsay's defense team focused heavily on what it says were major errors made by the various medical professionals who treated her. Her lawyers argued that they missed clear signs that she was in the midst of a psychotic breakdown and subjected her to an abruptly shifting regimen of drugs that only made her condition worse.

Zeizel, who was called to testify by the defense, said Lindsay was unable to appreciate the "wrongfulness" of her actions.

"She was unable to conform her behavior to the rule of law. She had no appreciation for the wrongfulness of her act," he said.

In closing arguments, Plymouth County Assistant District Attorney Jennifer Sprague shared the prosecution's theory of why Clancy killed her children.

"She was depressed. She was exhausted. She was done. She didn't want to try anymore. She felt damaged. But those kids — those kids were her protective factor. Those kids were keeping her from ending her misery. And so, she had to remove the protective factor. And I'm not saying she was happy about it. I'm saying it was what she had to do to end her misery," Sprague said.

The trial has brought renewed national attention to postpartum psychosis , a rare and poorly understood condition that affects between 1 and 2 out of every 1,000 women after childbirth.

"We know that we don't train our doctors in it, that it's massively missed," Dr. Veerle Bergink, a psychiatrist at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai in New York City, told NPR .

Dr. Susan Hatters Friedman, a reproductive and forensic psychiatrist at Case Western Reserve University in Cleveland, described the condition as "the scariest mental illness that I know of."

"You have these symptoms happening rapidly, you may or may not have any mental health history or any mental health literacy, and you've got this dependent little person with you," she said.

The case has also sparked a broader conversation about the shortcomings in postpartum mental health care in the United States, with women on social media sharing their own stories about not receiving the care they needed for more common conditions, like postpartum depression.

If you or someone you know is experiencing suicidal thoughts, call 911, or call the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-8255 or text HOME to the Crisis Text Line at 741741. (edited)
